guide.summary: Per-customer page reads fit OAuth 2.0 with a public integration, because scoped integrations can only be installed in selected workspaces. The least-privilege documented capability is Read content, which covers reading the shared page titles and content and excludes insert and update. Customers must individually authorize and share pages through the page picker, and client credentials and a redirect URI must be configured before the first test. Marketplace listing is not required to start authorization, and public-integration distribution review is not covered by the supplied sources.

findings.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization applies to per-user access
findings.detail: OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Each customer authorizes the app separately, and the app then uses that user's access token for API requests.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer workspace user connects their own Notion access to the app.

evidence.quote: a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

An OAuth integration isn’t tied to a single workspace through an internal connection API token. Instead, OAuth integrations follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol to authorize a connection to interact with

findings.title: Use a public integration for other customer workspaces
findings.detail: A scoped OAuth integration can be installed only in workspaces selected at creation and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Making the app available to any workspace requires a public integration, and installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces will connect.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading shared pages
findings.detail: The Read content capability lets a connection read existing content, including Retrieve page markdown, which needs read content and returns 403 without it. It does not allow Update content or Insert content. Sharing a parent page also grants access to its children, so the boundary is the pages each customer selects.
findings.appliesWhen: Reads titles and content of pages a customer explicitly shares; no page creation or modification.

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
provide access to child pages, as giving access to a parent page will provide access to all available child pages. Users can return to this view at a later time
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers must share pages through the page picker
findings.detail: The page picker shows only pages the user has full access to. Pages become readable only after the customer selects them and the authorization flow completes; if the flow is not completed, the connection gets no access to the selected pages.
findings.appliesWhen: A customer must grant the app access to specific pages.
